newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi relaxes curbs on Nigerians - paper.
newsitem.headline: Saudi relaxes curbs on Nigerians - paper.

text.p: Saudi Arabia has agreed to relax restrictions on Nigerians travelling to the kingdom and lifted a ban on those wanting to perform the annual pilgrimage or haj, a Saudi newspaper reported on Thursday.

The English-language Arab News did not give details on how the restrictions were relaxed, but quoted a Nigerian embassy official as saying Nigerians have been told back home they had until March 9 to register if they wanted to perform haj.
"Nigerians can obtain visas which will now enable them to travel to Saudi Arabia for religious obligations and rituals," it said.
Nigerian embassy officials were not available to comment.

Saudi Arabia last year imposed travel restrictions on Nigerians citing the meningitis epidemic that hit the West African country last year. It allowed in only 10 percent of the 31,000 Nigerians who had registered for the pilgrimage.
Arab News said Saudi authorities would continue to monitor the health of pilgrims arriving from Nigeria.

Haj, one of the five pillars of Islam which each Moslem who can afford it should perform at least once, falls in April this year. Up to two million Moslems are expected to converge on the holy sites of Mecca and Medina during haj.
